section.title: Step 1: poetry init
section.p: Action: Run poetry init; accept PEP 621 layout.

section.title: Step 3: Add dev group
section.p: Action: poetry add --group dev pytest ruff mypy.

section.title: Step 3b: Add test and docs groups
section.p: Action: poetry add --group test pytest pytest-cov; poetry add --group docs mkdocs, then mark the docs group `optional = true`.
Output: Four groups — main, dev, test, docs — with docs excluded from default installs.

section.title: Step 4: Lock
section.p: Action: poetry check --lock first; then poetry lock; commit poetry.lock.

section.title: Step 4b: Wire CI
section.p: Action: Install Poetry via snok/install-poetry@v1; cache .venv keyed by OS + Python version + poetry.lock hash; install with `poetry install --sync --no-interaction`.
Output: CI that reinstalls in seconds on a cache hit and drops packages that left the lockfile.

section.title: Step 4c: Multi-stage Dockerfile (if the project ships an image)
section.p: Action: Builder stage runs `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes`; final stage copies that file and runs `pip install -r requirements.txt`. See templates/Dockerfile.
Output: Production image with no Poetry runtime, typically 100-150MB smaller.
